SHW.rationale: Sherwin-Williams is a high-quality franchise with durable competitive advantages (4,900+ store network, professional contractor loyalty, ~49% gross margins, 14 of 15 quarters of margin expansion). Q1 2026 showed solid YoY growth (revenue +6.8%, EPS +7.5%) and beat consensus estimates. However, the sequential trajectory is weak—Q1 is seasonally the weakest quarter, but the QoQ revenue decline of -10.9% and EPS drop of -35.8% reflect normal seasonality rather than fundamental deterioration. The balance sheet carries meaningful leverage (debt/equity ~2.1x) from the Valspar acquisition, though EBITDA coverage is adequate. Valuation at ~33.6x P/E is mid-range of its 28-37x 12-month range, not cheap but not stretched. The upcoming Q2 2026 earnings on July 28 is a near-term catalyst—consensus expects $3.55 EPS (+5% YoY)—but this is a routine earnings event, not a special re-rating catalyst. The stock has recovered +8.2% in the past quarter, suggesting some of the positive Q1 beat is already priced in. Net: solid business, fair valuation, no compelling mispricing.
